product.name: What Argo does
product.line: It runs coding agents on one repository, draws their work as it happens, and lets you steer them.
short: Argo is a macOS window for one git repository. It starts coding agents there, and it also reads the agents you started yourself in a terminal. Every Session is a row in one roster.

In a Session you read the work rather than the result. You see what the agent said, what it ran, what it changed, and what it is asking. You type the next instruction, you answer its permission prompts, and you set how far it can go alone.
With GitHub or Linear connected, your backlog arrives beside the Sessions. You pick a ticket, press Start, and Argo starts an agent that already knows what to do.

Without Argo, a coding agent lives in a terminal window. Its work scrolls past, a second agent means a second window, and a question the agent asks waits until somebody looks at the right tab. Nothing joins that work to the branch it runs on or the ticket it came from. Argo holds every Session in one window, and keeps the questions in one place.

A room is one of the window's three tabs, and each one is a whole working surface rather than a panel. The three are Sessions, Tickets and Code. The window is in exactly one room at a time, and the deck draws whatever that room holds.
does: Start a coding agent on this repository, and keep every Session in one roster.

r-sessions.name: The Sessions room
r-sessions.line: You come here to watch an agent work and to answer it.
short: The Sessions room is where Argo opens. The roster on the left lists every agent Session in this repository. Select one, and the deck fills with that Session's reading, newest work at the foot.
The field under the reading is how you speak to the agent. The same slot becomes the permission prompt while the agent waits for an answer, so one place holds whatever question is live.
Argo started some of these agents and only reads the rest. You can type at the ones Argo owns. An agent from your own terminal stays read-only.
does: Watch every agent Session in this repository in one list.
Read what the agent said, thought, ran and changed, while it happens.
Type the next instruction, attach a picture, and pick a slash command.
Answer a permission the agent is waiting on, and set how far it can go alone.
Open a tool call and read the exact patch or output it produced.
Name a Session, archive it, and hand its work to a fresh one.

r-tickets.name: The Tickets room
r-tickets.line: You come here to pick the next piece of work and to start an agent on it.
short: The Tickets room fills both halves of the window. The sidebar holds the saved views and one suggested pick. The deck holds the backlog on the left and one open ticket on the right.
The tickets are your provider's own, read live from GitHub or Linear. Argo adds one fact of its own to each row, which is whether a live Session has already claimed it.
Start on a ticket and Argo starts an agent, writes its first instruction from the ticket, and takes the window to the Sessions room.

r-code.name: The Code room
r-code.line: This room is for the files and a scratch terminal, and it is still empty.
short: The Code room is the third tab, and it draws bare ground. The switch in the deck returns a clear color for it, and no view stands behind that.
The room is empty on purpose. A placeholder deck claims a structure nobody has settled, and every ticket built against it is then built against a guess.
The approved spec asks for a file explorer, a light editor and a scratch terminal. All three mirror the Project's working tree at its current branch. None of that is built.
does: Open the third room from the sidebar strip, or with Command 3.

r-connect.name: Connecting the project
r-connect.line: You come here to point Argo at a directory and to sign in to the services it reads.
short: This is a sheet over whichever room you are in, and not a fourth room. `CockpitRoom` names three cases and no connect case. The atlas holds it here because a person uses Argo to configure a Project.
It has two lives. On a machine with no Project it opens on Welcome, which says in three lines what Argo is for. Project Settings re-enters the same panel with one word changed on the button.
The panel is three independent rows in a fixed order — a directory, the two provider ports, and the companion plugin. You can complete them in any order, and none of them blocks another.
